intended_object: The standard bijection between the group-like elements of an R-coalgebra C (ε(g)=1, Δ(g)=g⊗g) and the coalgebra morphisms R → C from the base ring with its trivial coalgebra structure. A morphism f goes to f(1), and g goes to r ↦ r·g. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The forward map sends a group-like element g to the linear map `toSpanSingleton R C g`, which is r ↦ r•g. The proofs check that this map is compatible with the counit and the comultiplication, using ε(g)=1 and Δ(g)=g⊗g. The inverse map evaluates a coalgebra morphism at 1. The image f(1) is group-like because coalgebra morphisms preserve group-like elements, and 1 is group-like in R. The two maps are mutually inverse because a linear map out of R is determined by its value at 1.

This is exactly the textbook correspondence. It is stated over any commutative semiring R and any R-coalgebra C, which is its natural generality.

I searched Mathlib's coalgebra, bialgebra and Hopf algebra files on `GroupLike` and found no existing equivalence of this kind.
